memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then God said, "Let us make mankind in our image, in our likeness, so that they may rule over the fish in the sea and the birds in the sky, over the livestock and all the wild animals, and over all the creatures that move along the ground." - Gen 1:26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Something changes here. All through the chapter God has said, "Let there be," and things came into being. But now He says something different: "Let us make mankind in our image." There is a pause, a deliberateness, a special care. The making of human beings is not just another item on the list, it is the crown of God's creation.

And notice the astonishing words: "in our image, in our likeness." No animal, no star, no sea creature was made this way. Only human beings bear the image of God. This means you carry something of God's own likeness, the ability to think, to love, to choose, to relate to Him. Every person you meet, whatever their background or condition, bears this dignity. No one is worthless. No one is a mistake.

God also gives humanity a role, to rule over the creatures, caring for the world as His representatives. We are not owners but stewards, managing His creation on His behalf.

The wonder deepens in the New Testament, for Christ is the perfect image of God (Col 1:15), and through Him God is renewing that image in all who believe (Col 3:10). Sin has marred God's image in us, but grace is restoring it.

Whoever you are today, lift your head. You are made in the image of the living God, deeply valued and dignified by your Maker.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does knowing you are made in God's image change the way you see yourself?
2. How might it change the way you treat other people who also bear His image?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for making me in Your image and giving me such dignity and worth. Help me honour that image in myself and in everyone I meet today. Amen.
